      "stance": "objection",

  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "c:4030462014",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "reintroducing a generic LogPrint macro conflicts with the existing approach in PR #34038",
      "quote": "Concept NACK to reintroducing a generic `LogPrint`.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained macro cleanup rationale and proposed supporting NO_RATE_LIMIT flag; reviewer has not replied",
      "author_replies": ["c:4031481726"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:4031481726",
      "status_by_quote": "This bigger goal of this PR is to replace current implementation of the logging macros which is messy and inconsistent with a clean implementation."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2912164572",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "exposing the internal LogPrint macro invites helper patterns that mishandle rate limiting across log levels by silently dropping warnings or errors when info logs overflow",
      "quote": "this new macro may encourage to re-introduce helpers of the form: `[](auto level, auto msg) { LogPrint((.level=level),\"%s\", msg); }`, which will then work incorrectly with regard to rate-limiting",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "contested",
      "status_note": "reviewer pushed back in rc:2940897215 noting WalletLogPrintf as a real-world example, and author did not reply",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2912309418",
        "rc:2912485704",
        "rc:2912730565",
        "rc:2913416347",
        "rc:2913833312"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2940897215",
      "status_by_quote": "You give a real place yourself (`WalletLogPrintf`), where a dev (or an LLM) could apply the example today"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2940897215",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "exposing generic LogPrint introduces an alias for level macros, hurting greppability and consistency across the codebase",
      "quote": "Just as the logging was fixed to be consistent, so that one can call `git grep LogInfo` to find all info logs, this will introduce a new alias to grep for.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6161307494",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "whether the change in -loglevelalways output omitting category prefixes is intentional, and if help text and release notes should be updated",
      "quote": "Is this change intentional? The help text still says \"Always prepend a category and level\", and the `98f3bd6` commit message says there is no visible effect except in tests.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6161307494",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "LogDebug accepts invalid flag types such as plain integers or OR-ed masks, which compile but trigger runtime assertion aborts",
      "quote": "LogDebug now compiles when passed a plain integer or an OR-ed mask, whereas both failed to compile on the merge-base. For example, `LogDebug(BCLog::NET | BCLog::HTTP, \"x\")` aborts in a unit test",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    }
  ],
  "support": [],
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "author",
      "what": "responding to maflcko's pushback on keeping the macro internal and avoiding greppability regressions",
      "id": "rc:2940897215"
    },
    {
      "on": "author",
      "what": "addressing cyb3ralbert's findings on -loglevelalways output changes and LogDebug accepting invalid flag types",
      "id": "c:6161307494"
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Updated claims from schema 1 re-read. Marked maflcko's rate-limiting objection as contested due to pushback in rc:2940897215, recorded maflcko's greppability concern as a separate claim, and added cyb3ralbert's test findings as a question and an objection."
}
